author: kladar
body:
## Summary
Adds the `ieso_shadow_prices_real_time_5_min` dataset. 

```
from gridstatus.ieso import IESO
ieso = IESO()

df = ieso.get_shadow_prices_real_time_5_min(date="latest")
df2 = ieso.get_shadow_prices_real_time_5_min(date="2025-04-02")

print(df)
print(df2)
```

### Details
Currently these are not updating on the `public/` reports site, but they should hit any time now since they are on a 6 day lag. 

Prod: https://reports-public.ieso.ca/public/RealtimeConstrShadowPrices/
Sandbox: https://reports-public-sandbox.ieso.ca/public/RealtimeConstrShadowPrices/

Bit of a heady report since each report contains only one hour of 5 minute data, with the version number being seemingly synonymous with the hour (I don't actually use the version number for anything, but it could be that each hour gets more than one version/each day gets more than 24 versions). It could be that it has a more complex updating regime but we'll have to see how it actually updates once it goes live. This should get us 95% of the way there though. 

The code follows a similar pattern as adequacy report, getting the version files (w/ multiprocessing and retry logic), parsing, etc. For now it repeats that logic, but definitely starting to see a more general pattern that we could apply to some of these types of report getter methods.

author: zeke
body:
Every model on HF is guaranteed to have a task type.

As such, our current `models.ts` mappings don't need to have a manually entered task type:

```ts
{
  hfModel: "black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev",
  providerModel: "black-forest-labs/flux-dev",
  type: 'text-to-image`
}
```

Instead we can omit the type from the human-generated mapping:

```ts
{
  hfModel: "black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev",
  providerModel: "black-forest-labs/flux-dev"
}
```

... then use the Hugging Face HTTP API to fetch the Task™  (aka `pipeline_tag`) for each model.

This PR hits the API for each model, attaches the tasks to each model object, then hits the HF Model Mappings API.

## References

[MAJC-128](https://mozilla-hub.atlassian.net/browse/MAJC-128)

## Problem Statement

Currently, the way we specify our dependencies in `package.json` allows for a range of possible versions to satisfy the requirements. This can be a [security issue around supply chain attacks](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/cd152cb6742c5b8f2f3d2b5193b41d9c50905198/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies), and it's good to lock down our prod bundle to specific dep versions for consistency as well. 

## Proposed Changes

Pin to specific versions for `dependencies`, but leave the `devDependencies` flexible.

## Verification Steps

A step by step guide of how the PR reviewer can verify that changes are working correctly.

- [ ] Take a look at dependencies and make sure they are all pinned to a specific version.

This pull request updates the database schema for several inventory-related tables. The changes primarily involve replacing `uuid` primary keys with `serial` primary keys and converting foreign key references from `uuid` to `integer`. Additionally, some new relations are defined to improve schema clarity and consistency.

### Primary Key Changes:
* Replaced `uuid` primary keys with `serial` primary keys across all affected tables, including `assetLoan`, `assetValue`, `category`, `certificate`, `color`, `condition`, `depreciation`, `exitDetail`, `exitProcess`, `insuranceClaim`, `insurancePolicy`, `insuredAssetDetail`, `item`, `itemColor`, `itemImage`, `itemMaterial`, `itemType`, and `maintenance`. body: This PR removes `CoursierModule#mapDependencies` altogether, and uses `CoursierModule#resolutionParams` instead. `mapDependencies` is hack that the coursier API allows, but it's too powerful IMO. A benefit of using resolution params instead is that almost anything done via resolution params can be done via the coursier command-line, which is handy to debug things.

author: agocke
body:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/99576 changed the host to first
resolve symlinks before resolving the application directory. This means
that relative loads happen relative to the pointed-at file, not the
symbolic link. This was a breaking change made to match the symbolic
link behavior on all platforms.

Unfortunately, it seems a number of users have taken a dependency on the
Windows-specific behavior. This PR reverts the change and puts back in
place the old Windows behavior.

author: raomin
body:
## Description:

This PR enhances the ErriezBMX280 library to support using different I2C buses by allowing users to pass a custom TwoWire object (like Wire1 on ESP32 or Due) to the sensor constructor.
This change allows users with boards supporting multiple hardware I2C interfaces (like ESP32) to easily use multiple BMX280 sensors, even if they share the same I2C address, by connecting them to different buses.

## Changes:

- ErriezBMX280.h / ErriezBMX280.cpp:
Added a new constructor overload ErriezBMX280(uint8_t i2cAddr, TwoWire *theWire).
The original constructor now defaults to using the global Wire object.
Internal I2C communication now uses the provided TwoWire pointer (_wire).
- ErriezBMX280_TwoSensors.ino:
Added a new example specifically for ESP32, demonstrating how to read from two BMX280 sensors connected to Wire and Wire1 respectively.

- README.md:
Updated the documentation and example code snippet to explain how to use the new constructor for custom I2C bus selection.

author: mweinelt
body:
The comment says sha1, but hydra can deal with argon2id hashes just fine. Wondering what, if anything, creates that limitation.

The `hydra-create-user` script even has instructions how to generate such a hash.
```
Hydra uses Argon2id hashes, which can be generated like so:

    $ nix-shell -p libargon2
    [nix-shell]$ tr -d \\n | argon2 "$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc '[:alnum:]' < /dev/urandom | head -c16)" -id -t 3 -k 262144 -p 1 -l 16 -e
```

author: zacharycmontoya
body:
## Motivation

We learned that Java fails to do a correct propagation of the parent_id `p` when the scenarios is:
- Incoming tracestate has a `p` value
- A local span is generated that is a child span of the remote trace context
- The local span is injected into downstream headers

This new test asserts that the correct `p` value is injected downstream, which is the span-id of the local span.

## Changes

Adds a new test `tests/parametric/test_headers_tracecontext.py::test_tracestate_w3c_p_extract_and_inject` that executes for all languages, except for Java where it is skipped due to nonconformance.

## Workflow

1. ⚠️ Create your PR as draft ⚠️
2. Work on you PR until the CI passes (if something not related to your task is failing, you can ignore it)
3. Mark it as ready for review
    * Test logic is modified? -> Get a review from RFC owner. We're working on refining the `codeowners` file quickly.
    * Framework is modified, or non obvious usage of it -> get a review from [R&P team](https://dd.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C025TJ4RZ8X)

:rocket: Once your PR is reviewed, you can merge it!

🛟 [#apm-shared-testing](https://dd.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C025TJ4RZ8X) 🛟

## Reviewer checklist

* [ ] If PR title starts with `[<language>]`, double-check that only `<language>` is impacted by the change
* [ ] No system-tests internal is modified. Otherwise, I have the approval from [R&P team](https://dd.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C025TJ4RZ8X)
* [ ] CI is green, or failing jobs are not related to this change (and you are 100% sure about this statement)
* [ ] A docker base image is modified?
    * [ ] the relevant `build-XXX-image` label is present
* [ ] A scenario is added (or removed)?
    * [ ] Get a review from [R&P team](https://dd.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C025TJ4RZ8X)

- Refactors the clustering process to improve modularity and readability, reducing nested functions.
- Simplifies exclusion zone handling and raster processing, including flexibility for cases where args are not passed.
- Updates and refactors export functions.
- Removes the EPSG code parameter and updates related documentation.
- Updates README.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>google/yamlfmt (google/yamlfmt)</summary>

### [`v0.16.0`](https://redirect.github.com/google/yamlfmt/releases/tag/v0.16.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/google/yamlfmt/compare/v0.15.0...v0.16.0)

### Fixing yaml library stuff

This release features fixes for a couple problems in the yaml library, and one new feature.

### Features

#### Alternate Array Indentation

There is now support for `array_indent`, indenting arrays at a different level than anything else, and `indent_root_array`, an option to indent an array that is at the root of the document.\
To tell you the truth, I couldn't have possibly imagined anyone wanting this. It's quite outlandish to me. I decided to implement it because the request was well specified ([#​237](https://redirect.github.com/google/yamlfmt/issues/237)), it was very simple to implement, and it could be implemented in a completely unintrusive and opt-in way, without me needing to worry whether other parsing might break as a result. Given that, I figured adding new options couldn't hurt!

### Bug Fixes

#### Nested Indentless Arrays

There was an edge case where nested arrays would get collapsed when doing indentless arrays. This has been fixed now and should function as expected.

#### Comment Rendering Above Document Start

Comments above a document start used to end up rendered below the document start token with an extra newline. After digging into it I found out that this was a deliberate choice made by the upstream library (i.e. it was not in `libyaml` which that library was ported from) and I consider it an odd choice. I've changed it to work how one would expect, with comments above document start being rendered above the `---` token.\
I decided to make the change directly without guarding it with an option, since I thought the default behaviour was so odd and I can't imagine a world where someone wants it that way. But yaml is stupid, you never know if there's a random edge case I couldn't fathom that was broken by this. Hoping it will be okay, but might need a patch release if there's something I missed.

### Contributors

-   Thanks [@​abicky](https://redirect.github.com/abicky) for fixing the nested indentless array bug
-   Thanks [@​ELLIOTTCABLE](https://redirect.github.com/ELLIOTTCABLE) for the original feature request for array indentation and contributing to the development of it

### [`v0.15.0`](https://redirect.github.com/google/yamlfmt/releases/tag/v0.15.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/google/yamlfmt/compare/v0.14.0...v0.15.0)

### Happy 2025!

New year new yamlfmt release! This one once again only features things contributed by the community. I am working on a major feature that I was hoping to finish before pushing this release out, but I ran into a snag and I didn't want to delay these things getting released.

### Breaking Changes

#### New Minimum Go Version is 1.21

Originally I was keeping this library compatible with Go 1.18, which was the latest at the time. There was a time when I tried to update the minimum version to Go 1.20 when it was released, and I ended up getting complaints so I kept it where it was. Go 1.18 is long EOL, and it makes more sense as an application to stay up to date to in-support releases. So the new rule of thumb will be to maintain compatibility with the oldest non-EOL version of Go going forward.

### Features

#### `gitlab` output format

Generate yamlfmt results in [GitLab Code Quality report](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/testing/code_quality.html#code-quality-report-format) format. See more info [here](https://redirect.github.com/google/yamlfmt/blob/16479a1553068f709ae4cf439a2c893235662909/docs/output.md#gitlab).

#### `gitignore` match type

We had support already for `gitignore_excludes`, i.e. using a `gitignore` file to match which files to exclude, similar to how it works with Git. However, it can be useful for positive matches, i.e. what files to actually include, since the gitignore patterns can also be negated meaning that all includes and excludes can be managed by a single gitignore-style file. See more info [here](https://redirect.github.com/google/yamlfmt/blob/16479a1553068f709ae4cf439a2c893235662909/docs/paths.md#gitignore).

#### `yamlfmt` Docker image

`yamlfmt` is now available as a Docker image! This was originally done for the purpose of using `yamlfmt` in CI, but could be useful in other scenarios too. See download and usage instructions [in the README](https://redirect.github.com/google/yamlfmt?tab=readme-ov-file#basic-usage).

### Contributors

-   Thanks [@​octo](https://redirect.github.com/octo) for contributing the `gitlab` output format and `gitignore` match type, as well as improvements to the integration test workflow
-   Thanks [@​mrueg](https://redirect.github.com/mrueg) for updating the build and test flows from Go 1.18 to Go 1.21 and removing EOL versions
-   Thanks [@​fsrv-xyz](https://redirect.github.com/fsrv-xyz) for the Docker image work
-   Thanks [@​alexandear](https://redirect.github.com/alexandear) for doc fixes and test name typo fixes
-   Thanks [@​wusatosi](https://redirect.github.com/wusatosi) for the pre-commit doc update

***

I'm hoping my big new feature will be ready for the next update. Thanks for using `yamlfmt`, and thanks to all the contributors!

### [`v0.14.0`](https://redirect.github.com/google/yamlfmt/releases/tag/v0.14.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/google/yamlfmt/compare/v0.13.0...v0.14.0)

### Shoutouts To The Community Release

I have been in not the best health the last while, which is why this release took so long to cut. On the bright side, this release features more contributions from the community than from myself. Thank you to everyone who contributed!

### Features

#### `strip_directives`

`yaml.v3` does not support directives. The best thing to do would be to add some amount of support for directives, which I will do in the future just taking it as far as the parser not failing upon finding a directive. In the short term, I added a `hotfix` style feature that will strip the directives before formatting and put them back in. The feature is fraught with edge cases and only works reliably with directives at the top of the file. See the explanations I added in the [docs](https://redirect.github.com/google/yamlfmt/blob/main/docs/config-file.md#strip_directives).

#### `gitignore_excludes` searches up the directory structure for the nearest `.gitignore`

Arguably a fix, the `gitignore_excludes` feature will now look up the directory structure for the nearest `.gitignore` which unlocks monorepo usage patterns for `yamlfmt`.

#### JSON schema

The community has added a [JSON Schema](https://redirect.github.com/google/yamlfmt/blob/52c3b64ffcb1ad694aee768fd0969822c65b2b64/schema.json)! I'm calling it out in release notes, but this is not tied to yamlfmt releases in any way. If you have any fixes or improvements to make, they will not need to be tied to git tags being cut.

I am not super familiar with JSON Schema; I will try my best not to break it and keep it up to date but I'm not gonna be great at addressing potential deeper issues with it.

#### Validating releases with `cosign`

The release artifacts now generate other artifacts that allow you to verify releases using the [`cosign` tool](https://redirect.github.com/sigstore/cosign).

body:
# Description

- Wanted to integrate the warehouse transformer within the embedded destination transformer package (https://github.com/rudderlabs/rudder-server/pull/5828), but it is creating a cyclic dependency between:
  - github.com/rudderlabs/rudder-server/processor/internal/transformer/
  - github.com/rudderlabs/rudder-server/processor/internal/transformer/destination_transformer/
  - github.com/rudderlabs/rudder-server/warehouse/transformer/
- It also makes sense to keep the warehouse transformer package within the embedded destination transformer package, which contains packages for `pubsub` and `kafka`, as there is no dependency on the warehouse package.

## Linear Ticket

- Resolves WAR-629

## Security

- [x] The code changed/added as part of this pull request won't create any security issues with how the software is being used.

author: petrilloatwork
body:
Code should not need to link to service implementations, but only to their interface.
It is _art_ which will dynamically load the appropriate service per the job configuration.
This rule holds for services with multiple implementations (like `DetectorClocksService` and `DetectorPropertiesService`) and not for simple services (like `Geometry` or `WireReadout`).

A flawed seed in a single `CMakeLists.txt` linking directly to `lardata::DetectorInfoServices_DetectorClocksServiceStandard_service` has proliferated throughout `icaruscode`. The correct library to link is instead `lardata::DetectorClocksService` (which is not really a library, but it is what is needed nonetheless). This PR fixes all the faulty links to that service.

There should be no consequences to any level.

Reviewers:
 * @SFBayLaser because when I don't know I bother him

I don't know who else...

author: felipessac
body:
Felipe dos Santos Souza | Data de Finalização (08-05-2025)

## Descrição
Neste projeto, há uma forte ênfase em boas práticas de código, nos princípios do S.O.L.I.D. e na aplicação de DDD (Domain-Driven Design) de forma modular. Isso é mais evidente no backend, que está estruturado em módulos independentes (como books e users) e separado em camadas de aplicação, domínio e infraestrutura, o que facilita a manutenção e a evolução do sistema. No frontend, adotamos o padrão Atomic Design para organização dos componentes, dividindo-os por nível de complexidade (atoms, molecules, organisms). Utilizamos TailwindCSS com uma paleta de cores definida globalmente, onde cada variação tem um nome semântico (default, secondary, outline e etc.), aplicadas dinamicamente nos componentes com o auxílio das bibliotecas clsx e class-variance-authority, o que garante uma variação para cada componente estilizado.

Frameworks Frontend:
 - Next.js
 - TailwindCSS
 - RadixUI
 - Vercel (Deploy)

Frameworks Backend:
- Nest.js
- Prisma
- Postgresql
- Swagger
- Docker
- Terraform
- Google Cloud Plataform (Deploy)

## Decisões Técnicas e Trade-offs
Frontend:

- Utilizei `TailwindCSS` pela facilidade de estilizar com a integração da paleta de cores definida no arquivo global.
- O `Radix UI` foi utilizado para os componentes devido ao suporte nativo ao `TailwindCSS`, porém, sua estilização simples ainda exige a criação de um componente para reutilização quando necessário.
- Para consulta à API, utilizei `Axios` com `SWR`, que é uma funcionalidade do próprio Next.js para otimização e cache das requisições. Porém, o cenário ideal seria realizar esse tipo de consulta em uma rota server-side, com uma comunicação `client` → `BFF` → `server`, garantindo um nível extra de segurança no acesso à API.
- 
- Funções e estados propagados com frequência ou em componentes mais profundos na árvore de renderização foram inseridos em um `Context`, permitindo acesso em qualquer parte do `Provider`. Isso evita o “param hell” do `React`. Contudo, resulta em um `Provider` mais carregado, o que pode prejudicar a renderização otimizada dos diversos componentes internos.

Backend:

- Escolhi uma abordagem simples para os estados dos livros (lido e desejado). O uso de estados personalizados (dinâmicos) pode comprometer o controle e o comportamento específico de cada estado, uma vez que uma entidade pode ganhar ou perder comportamentos dependendo do estado, o que tende a gerar complexidade desnecessária, especialmente à medida que o sistema escala.
- Para atualizar o livro, implementei uma rota `PATCH` que, futuramente, pode abranger outros atributos com regras mais complexas. Neste primeiro momento, ela apenas atualiza o valor de `readed`.
- O `Prisma` foi utilizado como `ORM` por sua abordagem moderna, com tipagem automática, autocompletar e migrações simples. Contudo, perdemos algumas facilidades que `ORMs` como o `TypeORM` oferecem em relação à orientação a objetos.
- Foi utilizado um container `Docker` para garantir ambientes consistentes entre desenvolvimento e produção.
- Com o `Terraform`, foi possível realizar o provisionamento de forma simples e versionada (infra as code).
- Utilizamos o `Swagger` para gerar documentação automática e robusta dos `endpoints` da API, o que facilita testes e integração. Porém, os `endpoints` e `controllers` podem ficar poluídos com anotações e configurações.
- Seria ideal implementar pipelines de deploy, nas quais uma nova imagem da main e da develop seja gerada sempre que um merge for realizado, além da atualização automática das imagens em produção e homologação conforme a geração da nova imagem.

## URL de Deploy
link para a versão de [produção do projeto.](https://bookshelf-elder-frontend.vercel.app/)

## Como executar o projeto localmente
Para executar o projeto localmente basta seguir os passos destacados no README.md do projeto.

author: pradyuprasad
body:
Enhances the `sample_data_stratified` method to provide more flexible control over the sampling process and enable sampling from results that have been evaluated.

The `experiments` parameter type is broadened to `Sequence[Union[ExperimentOutputDocument, EvaluatedExperimentDocument]]`. This allows the function to process either raw experiment outputs or outputs enriched with evaluation results, and resolves a type variance issue by switching from `List` to `Sequence`.

Introduces an optional `filter_function` parameter (`Callable[[Union[SavedLLMResponse, LLMResponseWithEvaluation]], bool]`). This function is applied to each individual response before it is considered for sampling, allowing callers to include only responses that meet specific criteria. It defaults to a function that always returns True, effectively applying no filter.

Internal logic is updated to correctly retrieve experiment metadata and the underlying `SavedLLMResponse` from both input document types.

The `create_samples_to_label` method in the `KnowOrNot` class is updated to match the new, more flexible signature of the `sample_data_stratified` method it calls.

author: mrsr-odoo
body:
Steps to reproduce
===================
1. Install l10n_pe or l10n_se
2. Switch to the newly installed company.
3. Open the contact form. The address fields are misaligned.

Technical
==========
With commit https://github.com/odoo/odoo/commit/4dd27bba346e50f40769d1412fbca0b5f65bb5a6, the contact form renders address fields dynamically based on
the selected country. The `_view_get_address` method in the `format.address.mixin`
replaces the default address `div` with the XML arch of the view linked in the
current company's `address_view_id` field. Since this arch is wrapped within the
`<form>` tags, the JS framework adds an extra div element and `o_form_nosheet` class,
causing layout misalignment.

After this commit
==============
This commit only includes address `div` element inside the `<form>` tag.

Task-4744412

The `process` variable does not exist at all when the background script is loaded in Chrome normally. Resolve this in a similar way to the @hypothesis/lms repo [^1] by defining a variable using @rollup/plugin-replace instead.

Using `process.env.NODE_ENV` works in some of our other projects because they use @rollup/plugin-replace to replace it at build time. This is non-obvious from looking at the code however, so I think we should probably use a more-obvious custom variable.

author: chye0001
body:
This pull request introduces a new feature for generating and sending grocery lists via email, along with several smaller updates and fixes across the backend and frontend. The most significant changes include adding a new backend route and email utility for grocery lists, implementing the corresponding frontend API and UI functionality, and minor updates to existing components and error handling.

### Backend Changes

* **New Grocery List Route**: Added `groceryListRouter` to handle POST requests for grocery lists. It validates the request, sends the grocery list via email, and returns the data. (`backend/app.js`, `backend/routers/groceryListRouter.js`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-57fcf3bf0ff2ec3604e842595d8ac0b6a43665dac4d20b3da0136bd02dc36cd7R45-R47) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e89ee930cac85ab244caa56a1ceb3a30d48543289585966962cc13fbcf36323cR1-R17)
* **Email Utility Update**: Introduced `sendGroceryListEmail` function to format and send grocery lists via email. Updated the email utilities export to include this function. (`backend/util/email.js`)

### Frontend Changes

* **Grocery List API**: Created `sendGroceryList` function in `groceryListApi.js` to interact with the new backend route. (`frontend/src/lib/api/groceryListApi.js`)
* **Recipe Page Enhancements**: Updated the recipe details page to include a "Generate shopping list" button, which calls the new API and provides user feedback during the process. (`frontend/src/routes/recipes/[id]/+page.svelte`) ([frontend/src/routes/recipes/[id]/+page.svelteR14-R61](diffhunk://#diff-57363436e9a1f6186c3a901547f78503da3e950f3f5934e7253558c0cdbcff70R14-R61), [frontend/src/routes/recipes/[id]/+page.svelteR141-R148](diffhunk://#diff-57363436e9a1f6186c3a901547f78503da3e950f3f5934e7253558c0cdbcff70R141-R148))

### Minor Updates

* **Error Handling**: Improved error handling in `getRecipeById` to throw descriptive errors and ensure better debugging. (`frontend/src/lib/api/recipeApi.js`)
* **Default Values in Recipe Dialog**: Added default values for testing in the "Add Recipe" dialog, with a TODO comment to remove them later. (`frontend/src/lib/components/add-recipe-dialog/add-recipe-dialog.svelte`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a9b055ed01057b9523331fd47ebfd576315cb6473dce9e3e5ffb12d67170a17cR112) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a9b055ed01057b9523331fd47ebfd576315cb6473dce9e3e5ffb12d67170a17cL131-R146) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a9b055ed01057b9523331fd47ebfd576315cb6473dce9e3e5ffb12d67170a17cL154-R155)

author: micmurawski
body:
## Incident Response Training Exercise: Cart Service Memory Leak

This document outlines the changes made to the cart microservice to introduce a controlled failure scenario for an incident response training exercise.

### Changes

The following modifications were made to the `cart/server.js` file:

1.  **Global Array Introduction:**
    *   A new global array named `problematicGlobalArray` was declared and initialized as an empty array:
        ```javascript
        const problematicGlobalArray = [];
        ```

2.  **Data Accumulation in `/add` Endpoint:**
    *   Within the route handler for `app.get('/add/:id/:sku/:qty')`, specifically after a cart is successfully saved (`saveCart(...).then((data) => { ... })`), code has been added to populate the `problematicGlobalArray`.
    *   For every item added to a cart, an object containing `cartId`, `sku`, `qty`, a `timestamp`, and a deep copy of `productDetails` is created and pushed into this global array.
        ```javascript
        // ... inside the .then() block of saveCart
        const leakData = { 
            cartId: req.params.id, 
            sku: req.params.sku, 
            qty: qty, 
            timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
            productDetails: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(product))
        };
        problematicGlobalArray.push(leakData); 
        ```

### How Changes Affect Application

These changes introduce a **memory leak** into the cart microservice.

*   **Memory Exhaustion:** Each time an item is added to any user's cart, data related to that action is stored in the `problematicGlobalArray`. Since this array is global and there is no mechanism to clear or limit its size, it will grow indefinitely as users interact with the shopping cart functionality. Over time, and especially under load (as generated by `load-gen/robot-shop.py`), the Node.js process hosting the cart service will consume an increasing amount of memory.
*   **Service Degradation and Crash:** As memory usage climbs, the service will experience performance degradation due to increased garbage collection pressure. Eventually, the process will exhaust available heap memory, leading to a crash (typically with an "out of memory" error). This will render the cart service unavailable, impacting any operations that depend on it (e.g., adding items to cart, viewing cart, checkout process).
*   **Observability:** The memory leak will be observable through:
    *   Steadily increasing memory utilization metrics for the cart service.
    *   Potentially increased CPU usage due to garbage collection.
    *   Increased latency in cart operations before the crash.
    *   Error logs indicating an out-of-memory condition when the service finally fails.
*   **No Build/Static Analysis Detection:** The introduced code is syntactically valid and does not represent a pattern that static analysis tools would typically flag as an error. The issue is a runtime problem related to unbounded data accumulation in a long-lived global variable.

body: > [!NOTE] > Are you waiting for the changes in this PR to be merged? > It would be very helpful if you could [test the resulting artifacts](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/wiki/Testing-PR-Builds) from this PR and let us know in a comment if this change resolves your issue. Thank you! ### Root Cause of the issue - In the GraphicsView DrawString method, the behavior of flow direction for Arabic strings differs on Android compared to Windows, iOS, and Mac. - Android's StaticLayout automatically detects text direction based on the first strong directional character, causing Arabic text to render RTL (right-to-left) even when HorizontalAlignment.Left is specified. - Other platforms (Windows, iOS, Mac) respect the explicit alignment parameter and render the text LTR (left-to-right) when left-aligned. ### Description of Change - To maintain consistent behavior across all platforms, I restricted the behavior on Android by explicitly setting the flow direction to LeftToRight. - For Android API 23+ (Marshmallow and above): Uses StaticLayout.Builder with explicit SetTextDirection(TextDirectionHeuristics.Ltr) - For Android API < 23: Uses Left-to-Right Mark (LRM) Unicode character \u200E prepended to text as a fallback - Refactored text layout creation from PlatformCanvas.DrawString() into centralized TextLayoutUtils.CreateLayout() method - This eliminates obsolete API warnings and provides a single point of control for text direction ### Issues Fixed Fixes #17323 ### Tested the behaviour in the follwing platforms - [x] - Windows - [x] - Android - [x] - iOS - [x] - Mac ### Output | Before Fix | After Fix | |----------|----------| | | |

body:
Starting with CMake 3.30, FetchContent_Populate is deprecated. It can be replaced by FetchContent_Declare(... EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL) + FetchContent_MakeAvailable(). However, the EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL flag is available only from CMake 3.28 

This pull request checks the CMake version, and for versions <= 3.28, we use FetchContent_Populate, and for later versions, we use EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL + FetchContent_MakeAvailable.

author: lucyleeow
body:
#### Reference Issues/PRs
closes  #25639 (supercedes)
closes https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/21391

Thought it would be easier to open a new PR and there were no long discussions on the old PR (#25639).

#### What does this implement/fix? Explain your changes.
Adds a function that takes a scoring function, `y_true`, `y_score`, `thresholds` and outputs score per threshold.

The intention is to later add a new display class using this function, allowing us to plot metric score per threshold e.g.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33486b80-5c00-48e3-b7f8-de8d4ee0f514)

Uses the `_CurveScorer` as suggested by @glemaitre . Refactors out a new `_scores_from_predictions` static method, that takes the predictions. The old `_score` takes estimator, calculates `y_score` and passes to the new `_scores_from_prediction`.

Notes:

* `_scores_from_predictions` - name is inspired by the display class methods 'from_predictions' , but happy to change
* it did not make sense to use `from_scorer` because we are not using a `scorer` (which has the signature `callable(estimator, X, y)`) we are using a 'scoring_function` with signature `score_func(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)`
   * we instantiate `_CurveScorer` directly instead, and then call `_scores_from_predictions` in `decision_threshold_curve`
   * ~decided to make  `_scores_from_predictions` a static method, but I also could have made it a method, and in `decision_threshold_curve` instantiate `_CurveScorer` directly first (not via `from_scorer`). Only went with staticmethod path because I initially didn't register `from_scorer` instantiates differently than directly via `_CurveScorer`. Not 100% on what is best here.~ [realised that method is nicer to avoid having too many params in `decision_threshold_curve` and avoids some lines of code (use self.xx directly, instead of passing self.xx to `_scores_from_predictions`)]



#### Any other comments?
cc @glemaitre 

Lots more to do, but should get implementation right first.

To do:

- [ ] Add tests
- [ ] Add example
- [ ] Review `_decision_threshold.py` module docstring

In this PR, the following changes have been made to the URN parsing utility functions:

Tests have also been added, to verify that URNs of nested items can be parsed too.

body:
Fixes https://github.com/rescript-lang/rescript/issues/7438

In variant definitions without payloads, an error is reported if two cases have the same literal `@as(literal)`. The check so far was missing for cases with payload, where the literal goes into the tag. However it's perfectly possible to use the same tag in a case without payload, and one with payloads, as the two representations don't overlap.

author: elevran
body:
The original line seems fine at a glance, but `&&` and `||` have lower precedence than  expected in shell logic.
In some shells or environments, `command -v podman` might still run even after docker test succeeds, due to how the make shell handles command substitutions. Also, in a Makefile, using shell inside `$(shell ...)` can sometimes interpret spaces/newlines in odd ways.

Consequently, this results (on my Ubuntu, bash) in `CONTAINER_TOOL` set to `docker podman` even though only docker is installed.

CC: @clubanderson in case the same expression appears across repo's

body:
最適化シェーダー関連で下記の二つのAPIを用意しました。

|API|説明|
|---|---|
|OptimizedShaderGenerator.Generate()|最適化シェーダーの作成|
|OptimizedShaderReplacer.Replace()|Uberシェーダーを最適化シェーダーに置き換える|

また、アセットのインポートをフックして最適化シェーダーを生成していましたが、ワークフローを廃止しました。
新しいワークフローでは、最適化シェーダーの作成と置き換えをプロジェクト側でAPIを呼び出して、任意のタイミングで行えるようにしました。
また、最適化シェーダーの保存先のフォルダも選べるようにしています。

当初はNova Shaderの本体に最適化シェーダーを含めておいたのですが、初めてNovaを触る人がシェーダーの多さに困惑しそうなのと、カスタマイズの際に誤解を生む可能性もあると考え（最適化シェーダーまで編集する必要を感じてしまいそう）、今のワークフローに変更しています。

最適化シェーダーの作成は「Tools/NOVA Shader/Sample/Generate Optimized Shader」で、ビルド時にシェーダーを差し替える処理は「Tools/NOVA Shader/Sample/Custom Build With Optimized Shader」で行えます。

レビューよろしくお願いします。

These days I'm in a project to migrate from Sophos Proxy to OPNsense, nearly 1000 users, explicit proxy with ssl decryption and ClamAV/C-ICAP. There a couple of misconfigured site where certificate chain is incomplete and also not in OPNsense default stack. The only solution is to import by hand or ask website owner to fix it.

Now I had a new case where also importing missin certificates doesn't work and only option was this one.

To me it's fine as it says don't block connections when certificate validation fails, but we ignore this only for no-bump sites, so it shouldn't be a problem either.

author: nhantien
body:
# Configuration Management for Pipeline

## Changes

- Implemented centralized configuration management using JSON
- Added command-line argument support for config file path
- Created robust config loading with validation in `utils.py`
- Updated pipeline modules to accept config dictionary instead of loading directly

## Key Features

- **Flexible Config Loading**: Users can specify config file path via `--config` flag or use default location
- **Distillation Control**: Added `distillation_image_prop` parameter to control distillation dataset size
  - Supports both ratio (0-1) and absolute count values
  - Set to 0 to disable distillation
- **Improved Error Handling**: Added validation for config values and proper error messages
- **Better Separation of Concerns**: Configuration management centralized in `main.py`

## Usage

```bash
# Use default config location
python src/main.py

# Use custom config file
python src/main.py --config /path/to/config.json
```

## Example Config

```json
{
    "distillation_image_prop": 0.2  // Use 20% of data for distillation
}
```

author: lovedolove
body:
This pull request updates several GitHub Actions workflows to improve functionality and maintain compatibility with newer versions of actions. Key changes include upgrading actions to their latest versions, adding permissions for enhanced security, and modifying the release creation process to use a custom script for better control.

### Workflow Updates
* [`.github/workflows/build-installers.yml`](diffhunk://#diff-d705c049742d59d76f650c5555193909f9553044fd203d87c639a91905359a8aR14-R22): Updated `actions/checkout` to version 4, `joncloud/makensis-action` to version 4, and `actions/upload-artifact` to version 4. Added `permissions` to allow reading contents and writing packages. Introduced a `retention-days` parameter for uploaded artifacts. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d705c049742d59d76f650c5555193909f9553044fd203d87c639a91905359a8aR14-R22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d705c049742d59d76f650c5555193909f9553044fd203d87c639a91905359a8aL34-R48)

* [`.github/workflows/validate-batch.yml`](diffhunk://#diff-e8be8f99b61abf36ac2b5559400ca4d0627b1f0f3ce1a7df9df763f164884f50R13-R17): Updated `actions/checkout` to version 4 and added `permissions` to allow reading contents.

### Release Process Enhancements
* [`.github/workflows/create-release.yml`](diffhunk://#diff-8ac33fe295df086d3e55df1eb01194819d34cc0f5f54076dba96ceac0e40bd79R12-R19): Updated `actions/checkout` to version 4 and `joncloud/makensis-action` to version 4. Replaced `softprops/action-gh-release` with a custom script using `actions/github-script` to create releases and upload assets programmatically. Added detailed release notes and structured installation instructions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8ac33fe295df086d3e55df1eb01194819d34cc0f5f54076dba96ceac0e40bd79R12-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8ac33fe295df086d3e55df1eb01194819d34cc0f5f54076dba96ceac0e40bd79L38-R55) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8ac33fe295df086d3e55df1eb01194819d34cc0f5f54076dba96ceac0e40bd79R66-R101)

body:
This pull request enhances the robustness of the `ComponentDetection` class by adding defensive programming measures to handle invalid or missing `packageUrl` values gracefully. The changes improve error handling and debugging capabilities to ensure the system can handle edge cases without crashing.  The dependency submission API is keyed by package url so this scenario will prevent the dependency graph from having any information about this package.  

Fixes `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'Scheme')`

Seems to be a highly visible issue introduced with [component detection V5.2.16](https://github.com/microsoft/component-detection/releases/tag/v5.2.16) that introduced a new detector: https://github.com/microsoft/component-detection/pull/1388

author: see-why
body:
This pull request introduces enhancements to signal handling and user interaction in both the client and server components of the application. The most significant updates include adding graceful shutdown mechanisms for the client and server, implementing new game commands (`pause`, `resume`, and `quit`) on the server, and improving user feedback.

### Client-Side Enhancements:
* Added signal handling in `cmd/client/main.go` to gracefully shut down the client when an interrupt signal is received.

### Server-Side Enhancements:
* Integrated new commands (`pause`, `resume`, and `quit`) in `cmd/server/main.go` to allow the server to handle game state changes and exit based on user input.
* Added a helper function call (`gamelogic.PrintServerHelp`) to provide guidance on available commands when the server starts.

author: fw-bot
body:
Before this commit odoo/odoo@5bb76504425082cfd654a2860350aa94d9782dbd, the update query for UUID deduplication used [cr.split_for_in_conditions()](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/13133b40eb545c4d4f7427c2145b3d57074fa74b/odoo/sql_db.py#L402-L405) to chunk IDs properly for the `WHERE id IN (...)` clause.

However, after the mentioned commit, all IDs are passed at once, especially when `fetchmany()` returns up to 1 lac records. This significantly slows down the update query due to large `IN` clauses and memory overhead.

To address this, reduce the processing chunk from 1lac to 10k IDs. This reduces update time from over 2 hours to under 10 minutes in practice for recordset shown below:

```sql
apan_2760231=> select count(*) from pos_order;
 count
--------
 146885
(1 row)

apan_2760231=> select count(*) from pos_order_line;
 count
--------
 378860
(1 row)

apan_2760231=> select count(*) from pos_payment;
 count
--------
 184679
(1 row)
```

Logs:

Before fix (Almost 3 hrs):
```py
2025-04-17 07:06:31,094 31 INFO db_2760231 odoo.modules.migration: module point_of_sale: Running migration [1.0.2>] post-deduplicate-uuids
2025-04-17 10:08:39,397 31 INFO db_2760231 odoo.addons.base.models.ir_module: module point_of_sale: loading translation file /home/odoo/src/odoo/18.0/addons/point_of_sale/i18n/nl.po for language nl_NL
```

After fix (reduces to 10 mins):
```py
2025-04-17 11:29:44,294 23 INFO apan_2760231_18.0 odoo.modules.migration: module point_of_sale: Running migration [1.0.2>] post-deduplicate-uuids
2025-04-17 11:39:58,582 23 INFO apan_2760231_18.0 odoo.addons.base.models.ir_module: module point_of_sale: loading translation file /home/odoo/src/odoo/18.0/addons/point_of_sale/i18n/nl.po for language nl_NL
```

opw-4734894
upg-2760231

author: jumplink
body:
This PR significantly enhances the locale package for better integration with Weblate, improves translation workflows, and introduces new configuration and tooling for language management.

## Changes

- **Comprehensive Documentation**
  - Added a detailed `README.md` for the locale package with usage instructions.
  - Included a translation guidelines section for contributors (referenced in Weblate).
  - Documented both translation workflows: Weblate (for non-developers) and direct JSON editing (for developers).
  - Linked to official Weblate documentation in multiple languages.
  - Added a Contributor Agreement section to clarify licensing terms for translators.
  - Ensured license information is properly documented (CC-BY-4.0) and added the license field to `package.json`.

- **Translation Workflow & Status**
  - Removed all references and scripts related to the old Google Sheets-based translation process.
  - Added a Weblate translation status widget for live progress visualization.
  - Updated the testing checklist and provided clear instructions for testing translations.
  - Migrated usage metadata from Google Sheets to Weblate.

- **Locale Configuration & Language Visibility**
  - Introduced a new `availableIn` property in the locale config to control where each language is visible (e.g., callouts, backend).
  - This allows disabling languages in specific contexts until they are fully translated or ready for use.

- **Tooling**
  - Added a new `@beabee/weblate-client` package to facilitate integration with the Weblate API.
    - This was initially used to migrate tags from Google Sheets to Weblate.
    - The migration script has since been removed, but the client package remains for potential future use or automation.

- **Other Improvements**
  - Added French as a new language for testing  (A few community translations have already been added directly.).
  - Updated and improved translations for several languages (German, Dutch, Portuguese, Russian, Italian, etc.).
  - Cleaned up and normalized translation files for consistency.
  - Added watch mode to rebuild locale files on change

## Benefits

- Better onboarding for new translators and contributors.
- Clear, standardized documentation and translation guidelines.
- Improved workflow for managing translations through Weblate.
- Enhanced transparency about translation status and progress.
- Fine-grained control over language availability in different parts of the platform.
- Clearer licensing terms for contributed translations.
- Foundation for future automation or integration with Weblate via the new client package.

## Translation Status

Translations are now managed via [Beabee Platform Project on Weblate](https://hosted.weblate.org/projects/beabee/platform/).

## Testing Checklist

- [x] Add test translations for existing strings in German and German (informal)
- [x] Verify Weblate automatically creates a PR with translation changes (see #199)
- [x] Test merging the automatic PR and check if translations are correctly applied
- [x] Add a new language through the Weblate interface
- [x] Verify the new language is properly integrated into our codebase
- [x] Test the full process with a non-developer contributor (thanks to @NathanBnm)
- [x] Migrate usage metadata from Google Sheet to Weblate (The labels `User`, `Admin`, `System` and `CNR` were transferred to Weblate via a script.)
- [x] Remove migration scripts after successful migration (Removed [here](https://github.com/beabee-communityrm/monorepo/pull/198/commits/9935dcb21f8638b15ab299a524b579d5ae23d33d))
- [x] Add the option to disable languages as long as they are not fully translated (via `availableIn` property)
- [x] Add watch mode for locale files

## TODO after merge

- [ ] Set Weblate base branch to main
- [x] Request free hosting at Weblate

- `DELETE /api/upload/files/:filename` - Delete a specific file

All endpoints require authentication with a valid JWT token.

body:
## Description

Based on #3295 

I noticed in the debug logs of our staging server that some entries in the expiry table were never deleted, and thus they were processed again and again on each expiry tick.

This PR has the following changes:

* Bugfix: When upserting a packet, we were not properly clearing the *old* expiry entry! [This line](https://github.com/n0-computer/iroh/blob/f3c9af35542a7f2e00303090d1ca5273f86bc375/iroh-dns-server/src/store/signed_packets.rs#L148) is wrong: It should be `existing.timestamp()`, because that's the entry we want to remove, not the (not-yet-existing) entry for the timestamp of the *new* packet.
* Improve type handling and debug formatting around expiry timestamps, to make logs better readable and be less error prone to bad type conversions
* When an expiry entry is being processed, and the corresponding packet does not exist anymore, the expiry entry is deleted

## Breaking Changes

<!-- Optional, if there are any breaking changes document them, including how to migrate older code. -->

## Notes & open questions

We need tests around expiry. This should've been caught earlier. There's currently only a [single test](https://github.com/n0-computer/iroh/blob/f3c9af35542a7f2e00303090d1ca5273f86bc375/iroh-dns-server/src/lib.rs#L190) around eviction, added in the PR that added eviction (#2997). But that test only tests that expiry works at all. There's no test currently that verifies if entries in the expiry table are removed when a packet is upserted, which is the test that would fail without this PR.

## Change checklist
<!-- Remove any that are not relevant. -->
- [x] Self-review.
- [x] Documentation updates following the [style guide](https://rust-lang.github.io/rfcs/1574-more-api-documentation-conventions.html#appendix-a-full-conventions-text), if relevant.
- Tests if relevant: Would be relevant, but needs to come later.

Follow up to refactoring the generic utils mixin used in select-kit components in https://github.com/discourse/discourse/pull/32594. 

This PR follows a different approach as the util functions related to properties here aren't easily extracted without a major change to the interface due to the dependency on `this.selectKit`. It's largely a lift-and-shift with some minor refactoring of the conditional logic to reduce nesting and improve readability of the functions.

author: sriedel
body:
Billomat frequently returns HTML in their Bad Gateway errors, which bubbles up as a `JSON::ParserError`, making it awkward to handle in the calling code.

This is a naive implementation that handles a `JSON::ParserError` in the `Billomat::GatewayError` message generation.

My assumption is that if upstream returns a body in an error message, you may want to have a peek to see if it's interesting. However as a gateway error, it's very probably only generic error HTML, so we don't want to lug the entire HTML body around. Taking the first 128 bytes should be enough to see if the error body contains information that warrants further investigration.

Please let me know if you'd rather handle the issue differently. However it would be nice to be able to easily differentiate Billomat issues from other sources. 

As an alternative, a `Billomat::UnparseableGatewayErrorMessage` exception could be introduced.

author: kaspernissen
body:
## Which problem is this PR solving?

The resource detector for gcp did not previously support Cloud Run–specific resource attributes, although these are supported in other SDKs (e.g. Go, Java). This PR adds support for setting the `faas.*` along with `cloud.platform` resource attributes when running in a Cloud Run environment.

## Short description of the changes
- Detects `faas.name` from `K_SERVICE` environment variable. 
- Detects `faas.version` from `K_REVISION` environment variable
- Detects `faas.instance` from GCP metadata server (`/instance/id`) reusing the existing method.
- Sets `cloud.platform` using the semantic conventions static variables.
- Adds unit test for Cloud Run detection, following existing patterns
- Keeps full backward compatibility and aligns behavior with the Go SDK implementation (using env vars)

For more information, see the container runtime contract: https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/container-contract#env-vars.

This is my first PR 🙏 

I've added another PR for the extension of the `assertCloudResource` helper with `cloud.platform`. For now just manually asserting in the test case.
